title: chat.conversation.created
description: A conversation was created — written into the outbox in the same transaction as the row, so a subscriber never sees a thread that did not commit. Emitted ONLY on a real create: `create_direct` returning an existing thread is idempotency, not a creation, and a consumer that bound a domain object per idempotent retry would double-bind. Before this existed, nothing downstream could react to a new thread at all — a consumer learned a conversation existed only when its first message arrived on `chat.message` — which is why every binding of a thread to a domain object in this fleet was driven from the client that created it. `subject_type`/`subject_key` are the opaque pair the thread is ABOUT (empty on a thread about nothing in particular); `participant_ids` is every party at creation time.

subject_type.description: Registered subject type, or empty. Never parsed by this module.

subject_key.description: Opaque key within that type, or empty.

creator_id.description: Who opened it. Null only where nobody did (a system-opened thread).
